items.title: Google’s spam update vs. AI affiliate sites: An SEO experiment
items.summary: An SEO experiment created three low-trust AI-generated affiliate sites targeting commercial queries like "best welding schools," which initially ranked and generated clicks but collapsed to zero traffic during Google's December spam update due to programmatic content and lack of trust signals. The update confirms Google's spam policies effectively target manipulative tactics, rendering affiliate marketing viable only when paired with helpful, people-first content rather than as a standalone growth engine. Looking ahead to 2026, content strategies should prioritize fewer replicable pages, deeper insights, community discourse, and multi-channel distribution over SEO volume alone.

items.title: How to revise your old content for AI search optimization
items.summary: The article outlines strategies for revising old content to optimize for AI search engine optimization (AEO), emphasizing reformatting for topical breadth and depth via hub-and-spoke models, chunk-level retrieval with self-contained passages, and answer synthesis through clear summaries and structured takeaways. It discusses prioritizing content with expertise or proprietary insights that align with business growth, and adapting metadata like title tags, headings, and meta descriptions to serve as context anchors for AI systems rather than traditional ranking levers. Key impacts on SEO/content marketing include shifting from SEO's focus on traffic and keyword stuffing to AEO's emphasis on explicit, query-mapped answers and clarity for both AI models and human readers.

items.title: Google's Discover Core Update Finishes Rolling Out
items.summary: Google's February Discover core update, the first publicly labeled as such, finished rolling out on February 27 after approximately 22 days, starting February 5, with goals to enhance local relevance, reduce clickbait, and promote in-depth original content. Early data indicates increased regional personalization, fewer domains in top placements, and greater topic variety amid reduced publisher diversity. This update matters as Discover's traffic share for publishers has grown significantly, requiring prioritization of regional relevance, topic expertise, and original content.

items.title: February 2026 Google Discover Core Update Done Rolling Out
items.summary: Google's February 2026 Discover Core Update has finished rolling out after three weeks, starting on February 5 and completing on February 27, 2026, aiming to enhance Discover by prioritizing locally relevant content, reducing clickbait and sensational material, and promoting in-depth, original, and timely content from expert sites. This change may reduce traffic for non-US publishers targeting US audiences but could boost their visibility in local regions over time, with no impact on ongoing Google Search volatility.

items.title: Literary agents urge writers to avoid AI as they see 'change in nature of submissions'
items.summary: Several literary agencies are updating their submission guidelines to explicitly warn against using generative AI for cover letters and manuscripts, as agents increasingly detect AI-generated content altering the nature of submissions. Agencies like Greene & Heaton have added notes stating they will reject AI-assisted work. This move highlights growing concerns in publishing over authenticity and human creativity.

items.title: From Workshop to St. Martin's Press: How a WritingWorkshops.com Seminar Led to a Major Book Deal
items.summary: Stephen Harrison landed a nonfiction book deal with St. Martin's Press for 'The Power of Print: The Case for Paper & Ink in the Age of Technology' after attending agent Mark Gottlieb's seminar on crafting proposals. The book argues for the cognitive benefits of analog reading amid digital and AI dominance, pitched to fans of 'The Anxious Generation'. Editor Peter Wolverton acquired it, showcasing workshop success in traditional publishing.

items.title: Can You Legally Publish An AI-Generated Book? Exploring How OpenAI Can Write A Story And What You Need To Know
items.summary: Purely AI-generated books may not qualify for copyright in many places due to lacking human authorship, entering public domain. Human-edited or curated AI content allows copyright claims by the person. Transparency on AI use is advised to avoid ethical issues and ensure trust in publishing.

items.title: AI Models from Major Companies Can Reproduce Entire Copyrighted Novels
items.summary: Researchers extracted up to 95.8% of Harry Potter verbatim from Claude, with other models like Gemini and Grok also reproducing books without heavy jailbreaking. This challenges claims that AIs only learn patterns, not memorize, raising copyright infringement risks. A German court ruled similar actions infringing, amid Anthropic's settlements.

items.title: Censorship in the US: Book Bans in Texas Public Schools
items.summary: Conservative school districts in Texas are banning hundreds of books deemed inappropriate, following lists from figures like Ron DeSantis. Over 850 titles targeted, sparking debates on censorship versus content protection. The trend spreads across conservative areas, affecting public school libraries.

items.title: 'Yellowstone' spinoff 'Marshals' shocks fans by killing off major Dutton family member in premiere
items.summary: The 'Yellowstone' spinoff 'Marshals' premiered by killing off Monica Dutton, played by Kelsey Asbille, who died from cancer possibly caused by toxic pollution on the Indian reservation. Luke Grimes, who plays Kayce Dutton, shared his heartbreak over the plot decision and how the character's presence lingers through grave visits. Fans expressed shock and sadness, with some vowing not to continue watching, while others rejoiced at the development.

items.title: How the BAFTAs Bungled Its Response to a Racial Slur
items.summary: During the BAFTAs ceremony on February 28, a preshow announcement warned that attendee John Davidson with Tourette’s syndrome might make involuntary noises but omitted the possibility of racist slurs. Davidson shouted a racial slur as Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo presented an award, which aired to a global audience despite some editing. The event's handling has sparked criticism for insensitivity and poor preparation.

items.title: Carrie Underwood remains unapologetic as ‘American Idol’ backlash turns into MAGA battleground
items.summary: Carrie Underwood faced boos from the 'American Idol' audience while delivering critiques, responding defiantly by embracing the reaction and posting on X that she doesn't care. Speculation linked the boos to her conservative stance and performance at President Trump's inauguration. Social media divided, with supporters hailing her resilience and critics attributing backlash to her politics.

items.title: Valerie Bertinelli speaks for first time about being sexually abused at 11: ‘Nobody deserves that’
items.summary: Valerie Bertinelli revealed in an interview for her memoir 'Getting Naked' that she was sexually abused at age 11, sharing after years of therapy to release shame and express anger. She included the story to honor her younger self, shifting the book's focus from self-love. Bertinelli called for more voices to speak out against ongoing abuse.

items.title: Oscars organizers ‘scramble’ for red carpet backup plan amid Iran war: sources
items.summary: Oscars producers are preparing contingency plans, including potentially canceling the red carpet, due to the Iran conflict and Operation Epic Fury in the Middle East. The planned setup with Japanese maple trees for peace remains, but optics are under review amid sensitivities. Three Iranian nominees heighten concerns over potential protest questions on the carpet.

items.title: Barbra Streisand could make an Oscars appearance for a tribute to an old friend
items.summary: Barbra Streisand may appear at the Oscars to honor a longtime friend in a special tribute segment. Reports indicate discussions are ongoing for her participation amid awards season buzz. The potential moment adds excitement to the ceremony preparations.

items.title: Notion 3.3: Custom Agents
items.summary: Notion launched Custom Agents, autonomous AI that automates tasks like Q&A, task routing, and reports by integrating with Slack, Figma, and more, without coding—just describe workflows in plain language. Small businesses save hours weekly on repetitive work, enabling focus on growth, with easy setup via templates and free access until May 3, 2026 for Business plans. Multiplayer agents run 24/7, benefiting teams of any size.

items.title: Anthropic updates Claude Cowork tool built to give the average office worker a productivity boost
items.summary: Anthropic enhanced Claude Cowork with connectors to Google Drive, Gmail, DocuSign, and FactSet, plus customizable plugins for HR, finance, and engineering to embed workflows. This turns it into an enterprise-grade AI coworker, integrating real-time context to boost individual and team productivity without silos. Businesses gain admin controls and seamless tool access, making AI practical for daily office tasks.
